thread:
erin: Quick sync  We're iterating on SDK paging/stream surfaces. Main goals: simple ergonomics across Python/TS/Go, safe retries for paged mutating calls, and a predictable transport fallback chain. Thoughts?

paul: I'm leaning toward two primitives: Cursor for paged/unary flows and Stream for long-running generation. Cursor should be a small object with .next() and .to_token(). Stream is an AsyncIterable (TS/Py) / channel helper (Go). Keep them separate.

yuki: Agreed on separation. Important nuance: for pagination with side effects we must not silently replay arbitrary pages. Server should return a commit_marker in responses; client can only resume up to the last commit_marker. Also prefer server-owned opaque tokens.

tara: UX: for Py expose Cursor as an iterator and an explicit Cursor.to_token() to persist; provide a from_token() factory. For TS expose Cursor as an object implementing AsyncIterable and a .serialize() method. Go should have a Cursor struct and a Resume(token) constructor.

erin: Transport fallback order proposal: prefer grpc for Dedicated/Private; prefer http/2 (or grpc-web) for browser-heavy Hosted; fallback to http/1.1 chunking for environments that can't do http2. Allow explicit override in client config.

paul: For retries: split retry policy into two orthogonal flags: retry_strategy (none, conservative, aggressive) and replay_mode (auto_resume, require_manual_resume). Default conservative + auto_resume for read-only pages but require_manual_resume for mutating paged endpoints.

yuki: How will client detect mutating paged endpoints? Server should set a header or response field like "x-paging-side-effect: true". SDKs then default to require_manual_resume and surface a typed error when a retry would cross an unsafe boundary.

tara: Implementation detail: Cursor.prefetch(n) should be opt-in and bounded by max_bytes. Browser SDK should set a safe default like max_bytes=2MB to avoid OOM. Also provide a streaming-read API that consumes chunks as they arrive rather than buffering entire pages.

erin: Error taxonomy suggestion: PAGING_TOKEN_EXPIRED, PAGING_NOT_REPLAYABLE, PAGING_COMMIT_REQUIRED, STREAM_ABORTED. Map to typed exceptions in Py/TS and Go error enums. That unifies higher-level logic.

paul: One tricky case: simultaneous resume & prefetch race. If a client prefetched page A->B and then tries to resume from token X, server may reject if token no longer valid. Recommendation: prefetch should keep token lineage and validate before returning data; if mismatch, surface a recoverable "stale_prefetch" and give caller the option to re-request.

yuki: Telemetry: emit pages_fetched, prefetch_bytes, resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fail_reason. This will feed Optimize rules for recommended prefetch window and retry knobs.

tara: Docs + examples: need short idioms for common patterns: (1) iterate all items (Cursor until exhausted), (2) resume after crash (persist token, then Cursor.from_token(token)), (3) prefetch to improve latency (opt-in with bounds). Include small code snippets for Py/TS/Go.

erin: Action items: paul to author cross-SDK Cursor/Stream sketches, yuki to draft server response fields + error codes, tara to prototype a tiny browser prefetch PoC with fetch() + ReadableStream and conservative memory limits. I'll collate these into an API RFC next week. ci-bot: please add integration tests for Cursor token roundtrips and prefetch mem limits.

paul: ack. I'll include a small note about backpressure expectations for Stream (caller must consume; SDK won't buffer unbounded).

yuki: One more: expose "resume_supported" boolean on cursor responses so clients can detect if resume is possible at all; some ephemeral model modes may not support resume.

tara: Good call. That allows SDKs to surface helpful errors immediately.

erin: Thanks team. This feels distinct from our retry/pagination work earlier  — I'll open the RFC issue with sketches and tag you.
